page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.2xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at up to 3.9 GHz. It features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 32.0 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and requires remote EBS volumes, while network baseline bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps. Accelerated computing hardware is absent, with a zero GPU count.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded compute and text parsing capabilities alongside standard general-purpose throughput. In Geekbench testing, the server scores 2180.0 in single-core performance (top 25%) and reaches 2984.0 in text processing (top 10%), alongside an overall multi-core score of 8474.0. Single-threaded data compression is notably fast, with gzip achieving 34.38 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.47 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth registers 644.21 GB/sec on small 16 KB cached reads and 76.36 GB/sec on large 256 MB reads. In synthetic multi-core loads, stress-ng recorded 8671.14 and PassMark scored 15607.94, aligning with median multi-threaded expectations. Lightweight machine learning evaluation shows 288.8 tokens/sec for 135M model text generation.

The m8i-flex.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that experience variable CPU utilization, using burstable CPU scheduling to lower compute expenses compared to fixed-allocation tiers. However, continuous sustained saturation of all 8 vCPUs may run into burstable resource limits. The server is well aligned for mid-tier web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservices architectures, build environments, and general business applications that benefit from modern DDR5 memory and high single-threaded instruction rates without requiring dedicated local NVMe drives.
